newsitem.title: USA: Campbell Soup net hurt by $160 million restructuring charge. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Campbell Soup net hurt by $160 million restructuring charge. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. Wednesday reported lower earnings for the latest quarter, reflecting the impact of a $160 million charge to cover the costs of restructuring, including plant closings and asset sales.

The company said it earned $88 million, or 36 cents a share, on sales of $2.05 billion in its fiscal first quarter ended on Oct. 27. The results compared with year-ago earnings of $219 million, or 88 cents a share, on sales of $2.0 billion.
Campbell said that excluding the charge, it earnings would have been a record $248 million.
It said U.S. sales increased 4 percent to $1.24 billion from $1.19 billion last year, driven by an 11 percent gain in soup sales.
Bakery and confectionery sales, led by Pepperidge Farm and Godiva, were up 7 percent to $466 million from $435 million in the first quarter of last year.
Godiva Chocolatier also reported strong sales from continued expansion in the United States and Asia.

Campbell said it plans on Thursday to resume open market share repurchases under a previously announced three-year, $2.5 billion stock buyback programme. The open-market purchases are to follow a "Dutch auction" portion of the buyback, which was completed Oct. 10 and led to the acquisition of 13.5 million shares at $80 each, for a total of $1.1 billion.
Campbell's stock was up 37.5 cents at $81.25 in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
